lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You will hear a woman phoning the owner of a holiday cottage to make a booking. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Hello, Greg Walsh speaking.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Oh, hi. Is that the owner of Bramble Cottage? I found your listing online, and I'd like to ask about renting it this summer.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Yes, that's me. Happy to help. Can I start by taking your name?

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Sure. It's Emily Danforth. That's D-A-N-F-O-R-T-H.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Danforth, got it. And what dates were you thinking of?

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: We were hoping for a week in July. I was originally going to ask for Saturday the 9th, but my kids don't finish school until the 14th, so it would have to be Saturday the 16th, for seven nights.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Let me just check the calendar. The 16th... yes, you're in luck, that week's still free. How many of you will there be?

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Two adults and two children. They're nine and twelve. And I should ask, do you accept pets? We have a cat, but she's going to stay with our neighbour. It's really the dog I'm asking about.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: That's no problem at all. We take one dog per booking, as long as it stays off the beds and the sofas. The garden's fenced, so it can run around safely.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Oh, that's great. The photos of the garden looked lovely. Is that a lake behind it?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: A lot of people think that. There is a lake, but it's about ten minutes' drive away. The garden actually backs onto the river, so you can sit outside and watch the ducks. It's quite shallow at the edges, but keep an eye on the children.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Good to know. What about shopping? Is there anywhere close by for groceries?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: There's a small shop in the village that sells most things. The old listing said it was ten minutes away on foot, but they've since closed the footpath across the field, so it's 20 minutes now, walking along the lane. For a big shop, you'd need to drive into town.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: OK. So could you tell me the price for that week?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Our high-season rate is 850 pounds a week. But the week starting the 16th is just before the main school holidays here, so it's charged at the mid-season rate, which is 720 pounds.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: That's better than I expected. Does that include cleaning?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Yes, cleaning's included, and so are the bed linen and towels. The only extra is if you want the hot tub filled, which is 40 pounds, but most people don't bother with it in summer.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: And how do I pay the deposit? Can I do it by credit card?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: I'm afraid I can't take cards. I'm just not set up for it. And I'd rather not have cheques these days. So it has to be a bank transfer. I'll email you the details. The deposit's 200 pounds, and the rest is due four weeks before you arrive.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: That's fine. And how do we get the key? We probably won't get there until late afternoon.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: We used to have a key safe by the front door, but the lock kept jamming, so I took it away. My neighbour at the farm keeps a spare, but she's often out with the sheep. So the easiest thing is to pick it up from the pub in the village. It's called the Old Mill, and it's open until eleven.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: The pub, OK. And is there somewhere to park at the cottage? We'll be driving up from the airport.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Yes, there's room for two cars on the drive at the side of the house. It's gravel, so it's fine even when it's been raining, and you won't need a permit or anything like that.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Perfect. Is there anything we should bring with us? I want to keep the car as empty as possible.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: Well, as I said, towels are provided. There's a log basket by the stove, and you can help yourself to firewood from the shed, so there's no need to bring any. There are two adult bikes in the shed as well, but nothing for children, so if your kids like cycling, it's worth putting their bikes on the car. The lanes round here are lovely and quiet.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Good idea. They'd love that. One last thing. I'll need to do a bit of work while I'm there. Is the internet OK?

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: There's wi-fi in the cottage, and it works fine all over the house, upstairs and down. The mobile signal's the problem. Guests always assume it'll be better upstairs, but it isn't. The only place you'll get a decent signal is down at the bottom of the garden, by the gate.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Well, at least the wi-fi works. Thanks so much, Greg. I'll look out for your email.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: No worries, Emily. Speak soon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That is the end of the recording. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

layout.title: Bramble Cottage: booking details

explanation.correct: The caller gives her surname and spells it: D-A-N-F-O-R-T-H.
She first thinks of the 9th, but school finishes on the 14th, 'so it would have to be Saturday the 16th'.

distractors.why_wrong: This was her original idea, rejected because school has not finished.
This is the day her children finish school.

evidence.quote: so it would have to be Saturday the 16th

explanation.correct: She asks about the dog, and the owner says 'We take one dog per booking'.

distractors.why_wrong: The cat is staying with the neighbour, so it is not coming.

evidence.quote: We take one dog per booking

explanation.correct: The owner corrects a common mistake: 'The garden actually backs onto the river'.

distractors.why_wrong: The lake is about ten minutes' drive away, not behind the garden.

evidence.quote: The garden actually backs onto the river

explanation.correct: The footpath closed, 'so it's 20 minutes now, walking along the lane'.

distractors.why_wrong: The old listing said ten minutes, but that was before the footpath closed.

evidence.quote: so it's 20 minutes now, walking along the lane

explanation.correct: The week is charged at the mid-season rate, 'which is 720 pounds'.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the high-season rate, which does not apply to her week.
This is the extra charge for the hot tub.
This is the deposit, not the weekly price.

explanation.correct: Cards and cheques are ruled out: 'So it has to be a bank transfer'.

distractors.why_wrong: The owner says he can't take cards.
He would rather not have cheques.

evidence.quote: So it has to be a bank transfer

explanation.correct: The easiest thing is to 'pick it up from the pub in the village'; 'pick up' is paraphrased as 'collect'.

distractors.why_wrong: The neighbour at the farm has a spare, but she is often out, so this is not the arrangement.
The key safe was removed because the lock kept jamming.

evidence.quote: pick it up from the pub in the village
